statements.quote: In so doing, T-duality is cast essentially as a Fourier transform.
statements.reading: The letter's founding analogy: T-duality as a Fourier transform of string-loop functionals, Ψ̃[y(σ)] = ∫[Dx(σ)] exp((1/2πi)∫x dy) Ψ[x(σ)]; 'in the compact case, the Fourier transform is just implementing the T-duality'. It is the string analog of #11 §3's ρ implemented by the Fourier transform, acting on loop functionals. The record quotes this sentence (notes/literature-check.md §3).

statements.quote: The momentum may now be expressed as p=\oint_{C}\mathrm{d}Y , and so we will refer to Y as coordinates in momentum space.
statements.where: paragraph 'Quasi-Periodicity and generalized T-duality' (dual Polyakov path integral)
statements.reading: Y is called a momentum-space coordinate because its loop integral, its period around the string, is the momentum p. This is the sentence flag 64 quotes for 'the dual coordinates are the canonical conjugate of x'; in context it names the T-dual coordinate (next statements), not the conjugate of x.

statements.quote: Moreover these quasi-periodic functions are constrained to carry no dual-momenta
statements.reading: The 'dual-momenta' are the quasi-periods p̄ of X, i.e. windings (the letter writes p̄ = −α′∮*dY = 0). The letter's 'dual' is T-duality's exchange of momentum and winding.

statements.quote: Now, as suggested by the preceding discussion, we can introduce a momentum space coordinate Y such that \partial_{\sigma}Y=P . Like X , this coordinate is not periodic; its quasi-period Y(2\pi)-Y(0) represents the string momentum.
statements.where: paragraph 'First order formalism and the phase space action'
statements.reading: Y is defined by ∂σY = P, the momentum density (α′P = ∂τX in the same paragraph); its quasi-period is the momentum. This is the T-dual field: 1706.03305 defines X̃ by ∂σX̃ = ∂τX, and Y = X̃/α′ up to a function of τ (checked symbolically in work/dual-sector/scratch/r6-foundations/dual_field.py: quasi-period of Y = 2πp). Y's zero mode is therefore the x̃ that 1706.03305 finds independent of p and non-commuting with x. #11 P4–P5 work in one phase space (x, p); the letter's 'momentum space' is the T-dual coordinate of a string.

statements.quote: \eta is a neutral metric and H a generalized Lorentzian one
statements.where: paragraph 'First order formalism and the phase space action', before eq. (3)
statements.reading: FLM's generalized metric H is Lorentzian. #11 P1 takes H positive, and #11 §5 states the compatibility theorem it attributes to FLM for positive H (contradicts_record, last entry).

statements.quote: in which Born reciprocity is implemented as a choice of a Lagrangian submanifold of the phase space, and amounts to a generalization of T-duality.
statements.reading: Born reciprocity ('Born duality' in later FLM papers) is implemented as a choice of Lagrangian submanifold, the polarization language of #11 §3 and P5; the choice is said to generalize T-duality.

statements.quote: In this formulation both elements (\eta,J) of the chiral structure are dynamical. The solutions are labelled by bi-Lagrangians and spacetime is a derived dynamical concept.
statements.reading: The earliest statement in this set that η is dynamical (26 July 2013), 19 months before 1502.08005, which #11 P2′ cites for it. 'Derived dynamical concept' is not spontaneous breaking: the text has no potential, order parameter or vacuum selection ('spontan' and 'order parameter': zero matches in the full text).

statements.quote: Note that the 2d electrostatic picture of the correlation functions of the usual vertex operators [6] (see also [8]) now generalizes to 2d electromagnetism with electric and magnetic charges (dyons), if we allow vertices with both p,\bar{p} . The corresponding Dirac-Schwinger-Zwanziger quantization of the dyon charges is equivalent to satisfying the diffeomorphism constraint in the presence of these operators [15].
statements.where: end of paragraph 'Quasi-Periodicity and generalized T-duality'
statements.reading: The letter's only magnetic content: on the worldsheet, vertex operators carrying momentum p and winding p̄ act as 2d electric and magnetic charges, and their Dirac–Schwinger–Zwanziger quantization is the diffeomorphism (level-matching) constraint. These are string states, not magnetic monopoles in spacetime or in momentum space, and have no dark-matter role. My reading: a published remark relating the DSZ pairing to the momentum–winding pairing of string states, which bears on #11 §11.3's charge-lattice identification (flag 67), not on §11.4 or §12.

statements.quote: Given the interpretation of X and Y , this means that not only will space-time become curved, but momentum space as well. This then will lead to an implementation of Born reciprocity.
statements.reading: Letting H and η depend on both X and Y curves momentum space as well as spacetime: FLM's form of 'momentum space has its own gravity' (#11 App. A item 10), stated without field equations.

papers.summary: Introduces Born geometry for string theory. The string's target is a 'phase space' with coordinates (X/√α′, Y√α′), where Y, the 'momentum space' coordinate, is the T-dual field: its σ-derivative is the momentum density and its quasi-period the momentum. Born reciprocity is implemented as a choice of Lagrangian submanifold and generalizes T-duality; η and J are dynamical and spacetime is 'a derived dynamical concept'. No dark matter, no dark sector, no spontaneous symmetry breaking. Momentum–winding vertex operators behave as worldsheet dyons whose DSZ quantization is the diffeomorphism constraint.

statements.quote: when we talk about phase space, we do not mean the phase space of gravitational fields; we refer exclusively to the phase space of matter probes.
statements.reading: FLM's phase space is the phase space of matter probes, as #11 P1's is of matter; gravitational fields are excluded.

statements.quote: It is important to appreciate that this kinematical breaking is different from the dynamical breaking that arises in Schrödinger’s quantum mechanics, due to the choice of a particular Hamiltonian.
statements.reading: FLM call the breaking of Born's symmetry by gravity 'kinematical' (the preceding sentence: Born noticed 'that the kinematical symmetry generated by I is fundamentally broken in the presence of gravity'), as opposed to breaking by a choice of Hamiltonian. This is the sense of #11 §3's 'They treat the breaking as kinematical': it describes general relativity, which FLM propose to change (§1.3 below).

statements.quote: There is a preferred basis — the space-time basis.
statements.reading: The preferred-polarization idea in May 2014, before the 1502.08005 sentence #11 §3 quotes.

statements.quote: In pure quantum mechanics, H is a kinematical structure, while \eta or the choice of preferred polarization, can be modified by unitary dynamics. Alternatively, in pure gravity \eta is a kinematical structure (space-time provides a preferred polarization that cannot be modified), while H , or at least its space-time part, becomes dynamical.
statements.reading: Two regimes: in quantum mechanics H is fixed and η (the polarization) can be changed by unitary transformations; in gravity η is fixed and spacetime is a polarization that cannot be modified. Compare #11 P2′ (ω rigid, η emergent) and P5 (vacuum selection).

statements.quote: Moreover if we introduce quantum theory in gravity, we have to make \eta dynamical. This is our addition to Born’s argument [1].
statements.reading: Dynamical η is claimed as FLM's own addition to Born ([1] = 1307.7080). #11 P2′ attributes 'η dynamical' to [26S] (1502.08005, 2015).

statements.quote: Therefore a dynamical \eta necessarily leads to a relaxation of locality and a breakdown of effective field theory.
statements.reading: My reading: FLM use a dynamical η to relax locality (relative locality); #11 §3 uses an emergent η to explain why one polarization, and with it local physics, is selected. The same move serves opposite ends.

statements.quote: Moreover, the purely kinematical splitting of phase space into space and momentum space has to be made dynamical, and thus both the phase space metric H_{AB} and the neutral metric \eta_{AB} have to be dynamical in the context of quantum gravity.
statements.reading: The split into space and momentum space 'has to be made dynamical'. FLM's proposal is therefore not kinematical; it is dynamical without a selection mechanism (no potential, no order parameter, no 'spontan' in the text). Qualifies #11 §3 (contradicts_record).

statements.quote: not only a fundamental length scale \lambda but also a fundamental energy scale \varepsilon from which we can reconstruct \hbar=\lambda\varepsilon and G_{N}\propto\lambda/\varepsilon (in D=4 )
statements.reading: Two scales: a length λ and an energy ε with ℏ = λε and G_N ∝ λ/ε in four dimensions. The momentum half of phase space is measured in units of ε (§2: 𝕏 = (X/λ, P/ε)).

statements.quote: This means that G_{N} can be considered as a universal conversion factor between the seemingly different concepts of space and momentum space, in the same way that the speed of light is a universal conversion factor between space and time.
statements.reading: Newton's constant as the conversion factor between space and momentum space: the essay's reason for a second fundamental scale besides ℏ.

statements.quote: This null subspace is the effective space-time experienced by the string solution and is defined to be the Lagrangian sub-manifold with K=+1 . In this sense, different strings propagate in different space-time backgrounds which are made consistent via string interactions and through a dynamical momentum space [6], thus giving a sharp example of relative locality [5].
statements.reading: Each string solution lives on the η-null Lagrangian with K = +1, and different strings can live on different spacetimes, reconciled by interactions (relative locality). My reading: the closest these papers come to #11 P4's matter in another polarization; it is said of all probes, with no separate matter sector and no dark matter.

statements.quote: Since schematically \Box_{\eta}H=\partial_{X}\partial_{P}H , the last equation essentially says that the phase space metric can depend only on X or only on P . In the first case, we recover the usual graviton mode propagation on this space-time.
statements.reading: Linearized background equations □_H H = 0, □_H η = 0, □_η H = 0; the last makes H depend only on X or only on P, the first case being the usual graviton. The second case, a metric mode on momentum space, is implied and not discussed (my reading): the nearest statement in these papers to #11 §7 and App. A item 10.

statements.quote: Similarly, it has been argued that dynamical momentum space associated with Born reciprocity implies dramatic phenomenological consequences in the context of the vacuum energy problem [9], which also exhibits the mixing of short and long distance scales.
statements.reading: The essay's only cosmology-adjacent remark, a pointer via ref. [9] to Chang, Lewis, Minic, Takeuchi 2011 (arXiv:1106.0068) and Chang, Minic, Takeuchi 2010 (arXiv:1004.4220). Nothing on w or on a dual spacetime's curvature.

papers.summary: The essay states FLM's kinematical setting most plainly: quantum mechanics fixes H and lets η (the polarization) change; gravity fixes η (spacetime is a preferred polarization) and makes H dynamical; quantum gravity must make both dynamical, 'our addition to Born's argument'. Two scales λ, ε with ℏ = λε and G_N ∝ λ/ε. Strings on different η-null Lagrangians see different spacetimes (relative locality). Linearized equations make H depend only on X or only on P. No dark matter; one pointer to vacuum-energy work.

statements.quote: In quantum gravity, if all probes agree on what we mean by space-time, then we have broken Born duality — there is a preferred choice of polarization, the space-time one.
statements.reading: The sentence #11 §3 quotes, verified. The breaking is the existence of a polarization shared by all probes ('absolute locality' in the next sentences); no mechanism is given.

statements.quote: to unify both X^{\mu} and Y_{\mu} in one space {\cal{P}} (that we often refer to as phase space) and introduce a dimensionless coordinate \mathbb{X} on {\cal{P}}
statements.reading: The metastring's 'phase space' is the doubled target (X, Y) of double field theory, the same doubling as the metaparticle's Born geometry (x, x̃), not #11's (x, p). Bears on the record's contrast between foundations and metaparticle (contradicts_record).

statements.quote: \lambda is the string length which is related to the slope parameter by \lambda^{2}\equiv\alpha^{\prime}\hbar , where \hbar is the Planck constant of the worldsheet quantum theory.
statements.reading: λ² ≡ α′ℏ in this paper; 1706.03305 and 1707.00312 use λ² = ℏα′/2.

statements.quote: we can reconstruct \hbar=\lambda\varepsilon,\qquad\alpha^{\prime}=\lambda/\varepsilon.
statements.reading: ℏ = λε and α′ = λ/ε.

statements.quote: The Newton constant is proportional to the latter scale, G_{N}=\rho\alpha^{\prime} , depending on the dimension and the details of compactification.
statements.reading: Newton's constant is set by the string slope; nothing here on how a dual sector gravitates.

statements.quote: Note that X has the dimension of length while Y has the dimension of momentum.
statements.reading: Y has the dimension of momentum: the 'momentum-like' half of the doubled space.

statements.quote: Indeed, as we will see, for a boundary located at fixed \tau , \partial_{\sigma}X^{\mu} and Y_{\mu} are conjugate variables satisfying
statements.reading: Y is conjugate to the σ-derivative of X, {∂σX^μ(σ), Y_μ(σ′)} = 2πδ_P(σ, σ′), not to X itself. For the zero modes, x pairs with Y's period (the momentum) and Y's zero mode is a further variable (1706.03305).

statements.quote: A choice of Lagrangian subspace of phase space is called a choice of polarization.
statements.reading: The same definition of polarization as #11's (a Lagrangian subspace taken as position); η is called the 'polarization metric'.

statements.quote: Here neutral means that \eta is of signature (d,d) , while H is of signature (2,2(d-1)) .
statements.reading: H is Lorentzian here; #11 §5 states the compatibility theorem it attributes to [26S, §2.1] for positive H.

statements.quote: In the string case if the B field vanishes H is related to \omega via a complex structure. This is no longer true if B does not vanish.
statements.reading: The compatibility statement #11 §5 attributes to [26S, §2.1], verified; stated for the Lorentzian H of footnote 9.

statements.quote: Thus, the usual string theory in curved backgrounds corresponds to making the Q-metric H dynamical (but not the P-metric \eta or the symplectic structure \omega ).
statements.reading: Ordinary string theory in curved backgrounds makes only H dynamical; the metastring makes η and ω dynamical too (§2.3).

statements.quote: However, the Born proposal is not enough. As we have pointed out in [3], in the metastring theory we must take \eta to be dynamical as well. As we have seen above, it is \eta that governs the splitting of phase space into space and momentum space.
statements.reading: FLM credit dynamical η to their ref. [3], the 2013 letter; #11 P2′ cites this 2015 paper for it.

statements.quote: In the general case we promote (\eta^{0},H^{0},\omega^{0})\to(\eta,H,\omega) to be functions of \mathbb{X} .
statements.reading: All three structures become functions on P; ω is kept closed (non-closed ω is 'beyond the scope of our present discussion', §2.3). #11 P2′ keeps ω alone rigid. My remark: a closed ω that varies on P is locally constant in Darboux coordinates; the paper does not discuss ℏ in this connection.

statements.quote: In the context of the metastring, the rigidity of the quantum theory is encoded into the flatness of the polarization metric \eta , a metric in phase space that tells us how to define the notion of Lagrangian submanifolds.
statements.reading: FLM place the rigidity of quantum theory in the flatness of η and expect it to be relaxed on curved backgrounds; #11 P2′ places it in ω (constancy of ℏ) and makes η emergent (answer 'Other: rigidity').

statements.quote: We also clearly see that the 2-form \omega does not enter the definition of the string symplectic form. It only depends on the neutral metric \eta .
statements.reading: The string's symplectic form on the space of solutions is built from η: {𝕏^A(σ), 𝕏^B(σ′)} = η^{AB}θ(σ − σ′) (eq. 119); ω enters only for the zero modes (1706.03305 §4.1). My reading: η plays the canonical role for string modes that ω plays in #11's point-particle phase space.

statements.quote: That is, it relaxes the hypothesis of absolute locality and allows us to have a framework in which locality is relative, or, in colloquial terms, a framework where each string can carry a different space-time.
statements.reading: A curved η makes the split between spacetime and momentum space non-universal. As in 1405.3949, relative locality for all probes, not a separate matter sector.

statements.quote: The \mathbb{Z}_{2} component of the symmetry group is generated by J . This corresponds to the exchange of two Lagrangian subspaces.
statements.reading: T-duality J, a symmetry of the flat metastring action, exchanges the two Lagrangians (also §8: 'T-duality exchanges the Lagrangian sub-manifold with its orthogonal complement'). The other choice is equally lawful in the flat theory, as #11 P5 says of the mirror vacuum.

statements.quote: In the metastring formulation new CFT deformation modes are allowed, including the winding modes, whose collective excitations correspond to deformations of the \eta background. This links the relaxation of locality with purely stringy excitation modes.
statements.reading: η is a dynamical background whose deformations are collective excitations of winding modes (§1 adds that vertex operators in the spectrum 'are the seeds of deformation of the polarization metric η'). No potential for η and no vacuum value are given.

statements.quote: What is new about this viewpoint is that it allows us to think about the choice of space-time inside phase space as a dynamical question.
statements.reading: 'A dynamical question', the phrase #11 §3 quotes, verified. The answer the paper gives is the worldsheet-locality selection of the next statement, not a vacuum mechanism.

statements.quote: The condition of L -projectability is a target space locality condition specifying which submanifold of {\cal{P}} can be understood as a space-time. What is conceptually remarkable here is that this target space locality condition is selected by demanding worldsheet locality.
statements.reading: What selects spacetime in the metastring: worldsheet locality selects L-projectability, a target-space locality condition; quantum mechanically it becomes Λ-periodicity (§6.4). A consistency condition; it does not prefer L over its partner (my reading).

statements.quote: In order to formalize this intuition we define q\equiv x and p=h\tilde{y} and then we promote these variables to operators satisfying the Heisenberg algebra [p,q]=i\hbar .
statements.reading: FLM map the doubled space onto a Heisenberg algebra with ℏ. The symbol ỹ is not defined elsewhere in the text; from context it is the dual coordinate (my reading). This is FLM's explicit reading of the dual coordinate as a momentum at ℏ.

statements.quote: We mean that the area of the cell is \hbar , even if \lambda and \epsilon are the string length and string energy.
statements.reading: In (X, Y) units the modular cell has area ℏ although λ and ε are string scales. Consistent with the zero-mode algebra: in the 2013 letter's momentum units, Y₀ = x̃/α′, [x, Y₀] = iπℏ (computed in scratch/r6-foundations/units.py).

statements.quote: In the context of quantum mechanics, operators x and p do not commute and thus their eigenvalues cannot be localized within a cell of area \hbar . The modular variables [x] and [p] , on the other hand, commute with one another, and thus their eigenvalues can be specified precisely.
statements.reading: Modular variables commute and can be specified jointly: a modular cell is a polarization that is neither position nor momentum. Bears on #11 §3's mandatory-breaking premise (answer 'Other: modular polarizations').

statements.quote: In particular, one can easily see that, in the Heisenberg picture, the time evolution of such observables is fundamentally non-local, and that this non-locality is subtly hidden from us by the delicate interplay between the uncertainty relation and the compactness of the modular observables.
statements.reading: Modular observables evolve non-locally (FLM follow Aharonov): modular polarizations do not give local physics in the usual sense.

statements.quote: Any time we try to ‘compactify’ a direction we introduce a delocalization \emptyset\to[\tilde{x}] in the dual direction in a way consistent with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.
statements.reading: Compactifying x delocalizes x̃: the x–x̃ uncertainty trade-off, the analog of #11 §3's x–p argument. No matter is localized in x̃.

statements.quote: The usual space-time description emerges when the fields can be assumed to be approximately independent of \tilde{x} , that is when m>\!>\tilde{m} .
statements.reading: Modular-spacetime fields carry two masses, with □Φ + □̃Φ = (m² + m̃²)Φ and ∂·∂̃Φ = m m̃Φ (eq. 233); ordinary spacetime physics when m ≫ m̃, where dependence on x̃ drops out.

statements.quote: Consistent with the diffeomorphism constraint, we will in general have ‘dyonic states’ in the spectrum.
statements.reading: 'Dyonic states' are string states carrying both momentum and winding monodromies, not magnetic monopoles.

statements.quote: We expect that the metastring will offer new paradigms for particle phenomenology, for cosmology and for problems in gravity in which quantum mechanics and locality play a central role, and it may offer new insights into standard problems in string theory, such as vacuum selection.
statements.reading: The paper's only remark on phenomenology and cosmology: no prediction, no dark sector.

papers.summary: The metastring paper, #11's [26S]. The target is the doubled space 𝕏 = (X/λ, Y/ε), 'that we often refer to as phase space', with ℏ = λε, α′ = λ/ε, λ² ≡ α′ℏ and G_N = ρα′; Y has the dimension of momentum and is conjugate to ∂σX. A polarization is a choice of Lagrangian subspace, encoded by η; ordinary strings make only H dynamical, the metastring makes η, H and ω functions on P, and each string can carry its own spacetime (relative locality). Contains the 'broken Born duality' and 'dynamical question' sentences #11 §3 quotes and the compatibility statement #11 §5 attributes. The string's symplectic form depends only on η; FLM place quantum rigidity in η's flatness. Quantum mechanically the spacetime is a modular cell of area ℏ. No dark matter, no spontaneous breaking.

statements.quote: Given a scale, we can unify space and momentum into phase space, denoted {\cal{P}} , and introduce dimensionless coordinates x\equiv q/\lambda and \tilde{x}\equiv p/\varepsilon measuring position and momentum in natural units.
statements.reading: Here x̃ is the momentum p of the same particle in units of ε: #11's single phase space (x, p). The only paper in this set where the dual coordinate is the conjugate momentum; it concerns ordinary quantum mechanics, not strings or dark matter.

statements.quote: [\hat{x}^{a},\hat{\tilde{x}}_{b}]=\frac{i}{2\pi}\delta^{a}{}_{b}.
statements.reading: [x̂, x̃̂] = i/2π, which is [q, p] = iℏ with ε = 2πℏc/λ at c = 1 (checked in scratch/r6-foundations/normalizations.py, item 3).

statements.quote: \lambda , which in turn defines (given \hbar ) a fundamental energy scale \varepsilon=2\pi\hbar c/\lambda .
statements.reading: Here λε = 2πℏc, against ℏ = λε in 1405.3949 and 1502.08005: the papers' normalizations differ by 2π.

statements.quote: we propose to define Euclidean quantum space as a choice of polarization for the Heisenberg algebra of quantum theory.
statements.reading: Quantum space is a polarization of the Heisenberg algebra (a maximal commutative *-subalgebra): FLM's general notion behind #11 P5's polarization.

statements.quote: We show, following Mackey, that generically, such polarizations contain a fundamental length scale and that contrary to what is implied by the Schrödinger polarization, they possess topologically distinct spectra. These are the modular spaces.
statements.reading: Generic polarizations carry a length scale and are modular, not Lagrangian (answer 'Other: modular polarizations').

statements.quote: From this perspective, it is clear that the Schrödinger representation is not a generic representation of the Heisenberg algebra but on the other hand a highly singular one.
statements.reading: The position (Schrödinger) polarization is a singular limit of modular ones.

statements.quote: The concept of locality that we use in physical theories is tied to the choice of a preferred basis, the Schrödinger polarization.
statements.reading: Locality is tied to the position polarization, consistent with #11 §3's link between local physics and a definite polarization.

statements.quote: Thus we are led to the conclusion that general quantizations correspond to a choice of three structures, (\omega,\eta,H) where \omega is the symplectic structure that defines the Heisenberg algebra.
statements.reading: In quantum mechanics ω defines the Heisenberg algebra (as in #11 P2′), η fixes the polarization (a bilagrangian lattice), and H the vacuum.

statements.quote: In the context of modular polarizations, we show that there is generally no well-defined notion of translation invariant vacuum. Instead, we show that a vacuum can be identified with a state that is annihilated by a kinetic “Hamiltonian”.
statements.reading: 'Vacuum' is the ground state of a kinetic 'Hamiltonian' built from H; changing H squeezes it (§1.7, a Bogoliubov transformation). The vacuum fixes H, not the polarization; no vacuum selects a polarization (my reading).

statements.quote: A choice of quantum polarization is a choice of basis, unitarily equivalent to any other.
statements.reading: A polarization is a basis choice, unitarily equivalent to any other (Stone–von Neumann). In #11 §3 and P5 it is a physical vacuum choice; here it is not physical.

statements.quote: The space {\rm U}(d)/{\rm O}(d) represents the choice of inequivalent lifts \eta that preserve the symplectic structure and the vacuum state, while the quotient of the double orthogonal group by O (d) represent the choice of inequivalent symplectic structures, hence Weyl groups, that possess the same Hilbert space with the same vacuum.
statements.reading: The η compatible with a fixed ω and a fixed vacuum form U(d)/O(d), the Lagrangian Grassmannian Λ(d) (a standard identification): the manifold #11 §10 (Λ(1), τ's circle) and §14 item 12 (Λ(4)) use for the polarization. FLM treat it as a set of inequivalent choices, not as a vacuum manifold.

statements.quote: This is also the case in the double field theory picture in string theory where the target space is doubled to include winding modes but the space-time coordinate x and its dual, the winding coordinates \tilde{x} , are assumed to be commuting with each other
statements.reading: FLM contrast their picture with double field theory, where x̃ are 'the winding coordinates' commuting with x; in the modular picture the two polarizations do not commute.

statements.quote: it seems natural to suppose that the fundamental length scale is associated with the gravitational (or string) scale, \varepsilon/\lambda\sim c^{4}/G_{N} .
statements.reading: A conjecture (the paper calls the interpretation 'certainly more conjectural'): the cell's scale is gravitational or stringy.

statements.quote: This is a huge tension and all quantum experiments performed today, even the most energetic ones, fail by a huge margin to probe the thickness of the modular cell in the momentum direction. For all practical purposes we can then assume that the space is not modular, as long as we are not dealing with quantum gravity observables.
statements.reading: Why modularity goes unseen: a Planckian cell's momentum thickness is beyond experiment. The argument concerns the modularity of space, not a dark sector or the null results of direct detection.

statements.quote: It is quite possible that the structure of modular quantizations has observable consequences in metastring theory, through UV-IR mixing, when the appropriate limit is taken to obtain local effective field theories in large space-times.
statements.reading: Possible observable consequences through UV–IR mixing; no specific prediction.

papers.summary: Ordinary quantum mechanics, no strings. Phase space (q, p) in units λ and ε = 2πℏc/λ, with x̃ ≡ p/ε and [x̂, x̃̂] = i/2π: here the dual coordinate is the momentum of the same particle. Quantum space is defined as a polarization (maximal commutative subalgebra) of the Heisenberg algebra; generic polarizations are modular, with a length scale, and the Schrödinger polarization is singular. A quantization needs (ω, η, H): ω defines the algebra, η the polarization, H the vacuum. A polarization is a basis choice, unitarily equivalent to any other; the space of η at fixed ω and vacuum is U(d)/O(d). No dark matter.

answers.question: Q1
answers.answer: Not addressed in these papers. None of the seven (posted 26 July 2013 to 27 December 2018) mentions dark matter: tools/lit.py text --grep 'dark' finds zero matches in each full text. None states, proposes or speculates that dark matter is the dual or conjugate counterpart of visible matter. The nearest content is the metaparticle's 'dual particle, dual anti-particle pair' (1812.10821 §3.2), two further poles of the same propagator related to the particle pair by E ↔ μ/E, which 'corresponds to the exchange of p with p̃'; ordinary particles are the sector with μ = 0 and vanishing dual momentum p̃, 'a consistent truncation' preserved by interactions (§2.1). Neither is given a dark-matter role. This agrees with the record's dating of the school's identification to Minic 2020 (arXiv:2003.00318), which these papers precede; I did not read Minic 2020.

answers.question: Q2
answers.answer: It depends on the paper. (a) Ordinary quantum mechanics, 1606.01829 §1.1: x ≡ q/λ and x̃ ≡ p/ε 'measuring position and momentum in natural units', with ε = 2πℏc/λ and [x̂, x̃̂] = i/2π, which is [q, p] = iℏ (checked, normalizations.py). Here x̃ is the canonical momentum of the same particle at ℏ, as in #11's one phase space (x, p). (b) The string papers: the target 'phase space' is the doubled space 𝕏 = (X/λ, Y/ε) (1502.08005 eq. 13; (X/√α′, Y√α′) in 1307.7080). Y is 'a momentum space coordinate' defined by ∂σY = P, the momentum density; its quasi-period around the string is the momentum (1307.7080); it has the dimension of momentum and is conjugate to ∂σX, not to X (1502.08005 eqs. 6–7). It is the T-dual field: 1706.03305 defines X̃ by ∂σX̃ = ∂τX, and Y = X̃/α′ up to a function of τ (dual_field.py). The zero modes x = x_R + x_L, x̃ = x_R − x_L, p, p̃ are independent, with [x̂, p̂] = iℏ = [x̃̂, p̃̂], [p̂, p̃̂] = 0 and [x̂, x̃̂] = 2πiλ², λ = √(ℏα′/2), i.e. iπℏα′ (1706.03305 eq. 73; 1707.00312 eqs. 5–6). The canonical pairs are (p, x) and (p̃, x̃ − πα′p) (1706.03305 eq. 69): x̃ = q̃ + πα′p, with q̃ conjugate to the winding p̃ and commuting with x. So x̃ is a coordinate of a doubled space, conjugate (through q̃) to winding, which contains πα′ times the ordinary momentum and therefore does not commute with x. In x̃'s length units the commutator is 'set by the string length scale' (1706.03305 abstract) and independent of the radius (§3); in Y's momentum units it is [x, Y₀] = iπℏ (units.py), and 1502.08005 fn. 32 gives the modular cell area ℏ. FLM read (x, x̃) as a Heisenberg pair: 'the double space P should be understood as a phase space' (1706.03305 §4.1); in 1502.08005 §7.2 they set q ≡ x, p = hỹ, [p, q] = iℏ. (c) The metaparticle, 1812.10821 §2: phase space {x, p, x̃, p̃} with {p, x} = 1, {p̃, x̃} = 1, {x̃, x} = πα′ (Darboux as α′ → 0); in the convention [x, p] = iℏ this is [x, x̃] = iπℏα′, the same as 1706.03305 (normalizations.py). Scales: ℏ = λε, α′ = λ/ε, λ² ≡ α′ℏ, G_N = ρα′ (1502.08005 eq. 4); ℏ = λε, G_N ∝ λ/ε in D = 4 (1405.3949 §1.3); ε = 2πℏc/λ (1606.01829 §1.1); λ = √(ℏα′/2) (1706.03305 eq. 5; 1707.00312 §2). These normalizations differ by factors 2 and 2π. Compared with the program: χ lives in the p-polarization of one phase space (x, p) with ω rigid (#11 P2′, P4, P5). In the string and metaparticle papers the dual polarization is that of x̃, a partner of x in a doubled space, while the ordinary p remains a separate variable; only 1606.01829 has the program's setting, and it is not about strings or dark matter.

answers.question: Q3
answers.answer: No dual Standard Model, no dual photon and no dual charges appear in these papers. What they have: the metaparticle's dual particle/dual anti-particle pair, two further poles of one propagator (1812.10821 §3.2, §6); string states carrying both momentum and winding, which on the worldsheet act as electric and magnetic charges ('2d electromagnetism with electric and magnetic charges (dyons)', 1307.7080; 'dyonic states', 1502.08005 §1); and fields Φ(x, x̃) on modular spacetime with two masses (m, m̃), the usual spacetime description holding when m ≫ m̃ (1502.08005 §7.3). Fields 'living in the dual space' (1707.00312 §3) are the same states in another basis: 'one should simply choose one or the other ... the difference being simply a change of basis'. The metaparticle's two chiral components are 'entangled' in a way that 'prevents an interpretation as two particle species' (1812.10821 §3.1). Nothing assigns a matter species to the dual polarization, as #11 P4 does (x-polarized Standard Model, p-polarized χ) or #11 §11.4's magnetic mirror would.

answers.question: Q4
answers.answer: Not addressed as a coupling between a dark and a visible sector: there is no dark sector in these papers. What they say about links between x and x̃ and about decoupling: (1) x and x̃ are linked kinematically by [x, x̃] = 2πiλ² (1706.03305 eq. 73), independent of the radius (§3) and present in trivial backgrounds; in the metaparticle it disappears only as α′ → 0 (1812.10821 §2). (2) The dual degrees of freedom decouple in limits: R → ∞ projects p̃ → 0 and x̃ decouples (1706.03305 §2; 1707.00312 §2); ordinary spacetime physics when m ≫ m̃ (1502.08005 §7.3). (3) Interactions: the closed-string product conserves momentum and winding, with a phase exp(iπw′(n − n′)) (1707.00312 §4, eq. 41); the metaparticle's p̃ is conserved, and ordinary particles (μ = 0, p̃ = 0) form 'a consistent truncation ... preserved by the interactions' (1812.10821 §2.1); particle-number-changing metaparticle interactions are not developed (§5). (4) 'Entanglement' appears once, for the two chiral components of a single metaparticle (1812.10821 §3.1); 'correlated' is never used for a dark–visible relation. My inference: (3) makes p̃ a conserved label, so a p̃ = 0 sector does not feed p̃ ≠ 0 states through p̃-conserving interactions; this is a selection rule, not a coupling strength. None of this is #11 P4's gravity-only coupling or its opposite; the later 'correlated' dark sector the record attributes to the school (notes/literature-check.md §3) is not defined in these papers.

answers.question: Q5
answers.answer: Not addressed for dark matter: no direct-detection, collider or galactic prediction and no acceleration scale. 1502.08005 §8 expects 'new paradigms for particle phenomenology, for cosmology' without specifics. 1606.01829 gives a reason modular structure goes unseen: if the cell is Planckian, 'all quantum experiments performed today ... fail by a huge margin to probe the thickness of the modular cell in the momentum direction' (§1.4); it allows 'observable consequences ... through UV-IR mixing' (§3). That argument concerns the modularity of space, not a dark sector or the null results of direct detection.

answers.question: Q6
answers.answer: How a dual sector gravitates is not addressed. On gravity and Newton's constant: G_N ∝ λ/ε in four dimensions, 'a universal conversion factor between ... space and momentum space' (1405.3949 §1.2–§1.3); G_N = ρα′, 'depending on the dimension and the details of compactification' (1502.08005 eq. 4); conjecturally ε/λ ∼ c⁴/G_N, the cell scale being 'the gravitational (or string) scale' (1606.01829 §3). Ordinary curved-background string theory makes H dynamical but not η or ω (1502.08005 §2.1). The 2014 essay's linearized equations □_H H = 0, □_H η = 0, □_η H = 0 make the phase-space metric depend 'only on X or only on P', the first case being 'the usual graviton mode' (1405.3949 §2.2); the second case, a metric mode depending only on P, is implied and not discussed (my reading). With 1307.7080's 'not only will space-time become curved, but momentum space as well', this is the nearest these papers come to #11 App. A item 10 and §7's momentum-space gravity; no massive spin-2 field and nothing like X appears.

answers.question: Q7
answers.answer: Not addressed for a dark sector: no self-interaction, no dependence on relative velocity, no localization of matter in x̃ or in momentum, no condensate or wave form. Related dynamics: the metaparticle constraint p·p̃ = μ fixes 'the component of the momentum parallel to p̃' of each particle (1812.10821 §2.1); p̃ is conserved, and metaparticles with different p̃ have different dispersion relations and 'de facto effectively experience different notions of space-time' (§2.1); ordinary particles (p̃ = 0) form a consistent truncation preserved by interactions; particle-number-changing interactions are left to future work and only background gauge fields are coupled (§5). An INSPIRE search of titles and abstracts for 'metaparticle' returns five papers (1812.10821, Minic 2020, Barnes–Heremans–Minic 2021, two by Chouha 2026), none developing metaparticle interactions. Closed-string interactions conserve momentum and winding and carry a phase depending on both (1707.00312 eq. 41). My reading: nothing here acts as a gate in relative momentum. Conservation of p̃ restricts which total p̃ can appear; it does not suppress scattering as the relative momentum grows, and it is not #11 §8's knee at v*. Localization: compactifying x delocalizes x̃ 'consistent with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle' (1502.08005 §7.4); the modular cell is these papers' localization concept, for space, not for matter.

answers.question: Q8
answers.answer: No magnetically charged or dyonic objects as matter, and nothing localized in x̃ or in momentum. Magnetic language appears in three ways. (1) On the worldsheet, vertex operators with momentum p and winding p̄ act as 2d 'electric and magnetic charges (dyons)', and 'the Dirac-Schwinger-Zwanziger quantization of the dyon charges is equivalent to satisfying the diffeomorphism constraint' (1307.7080); the metastring spectrum has 'dyonic states' (1502.08005 §1). (2) Algebraic analogies: the zero-mode algebra 'has an analogy in electromagnetism in the presence of monopoles', with the string length as magnetic length and ω as magnetic field (1707.00312 §5.1 fn. 10); the metaparticle brackets resemble Dirac brackets 'reduced to the lowest Landau level' (1812.10821 §2 fn. 5); 1606.01829 §1.5 likens a modular space to a phase-space torus with a constant magnetic field. (3) None is dark matter. My reading: (1) is a published remark tying the DSZ pairing to the momentum–winding pairing of string states; it bears on #11 §11.3's identification of the charge lattice's DSZ form with a symplectic polarization (flag 67), not on §11.4's magnetic mirror or §12's conjugate monopoles.

answers.question: Q9
answers.answer: Definitions. A polarization is 'a choice of Lagrangian subspace of phase space' (1502.08005 §2), encoded by the neutral 'polarization metric' η, with spacetime L = ker(η + ω) and momentum space L̃ = ker(η − ω) (§2.1); quantum space is 'a choice of polarization for the Heisenberg algebra', a maximal commutative subalgebra, generically modular (1606.01829); spacetime is the η-null Lagrangian with K = +1 (1405.3949 §2). What selects it. (1) In general relativity and the usual string η is kinematical: 'space-time provides a preferred polarization that cannot be modified' (1405.3949 §1.3); 'There is a preferred basis — the space-time basis' (§1.1). (2) FLM propose making the split dynamical: η and J dynamical, 'spacetime is a derived dynamical concept' (1307.7080, 26 July 2013); 'the purely kinematical splitting ... has to be made dynamical' (1405.3949); 'the choice of space-time inside phase space as a dynamical question' (1502.08005 §7); η's deformations are collective excitations of winding modes (§8). (3) A concrete selection: worldsheet locality selects the target-space locality condition (L-projectability; quantum mechanically Λ-periodicity) that makes a Lagrangian spacetime (1502.08005 §6.4, §7). (4) For the compact string the radius decides: 'which compact coordinate, x or x̃, plays the role of a spatial coordinate depends on context' (1707.00312 §2), x at large R and x̃ at small R; T-dualities 'change the choice of polarization' (1706.03305 §5). (5) In quantum mechanics and in the metaparticle the choice is a basis or analysis choice: 'A choice of quantum polarization is a choice of basis, unitarily equivalent to any other' (1606.01829 §3); the metaparticle is studied in the (x, p̃) polarization, with 'nothing special about the x^μ' (1812.10821 §2). Spontaneous? No: 'spontan' and 'order parameter' have zero matches in all seven texts; there is no potential for η and no symmetry-breaking vacuum. 'Vacuum' in 1606.01829 is the ground state of a kinetic 'Hamiltonian' built from H, squeezed when H changes (§1.7); it does not select η. The η compatible with a fixed ω and a fixed vacuum form U(d)/O(d) (1606.01829 §2), the Lagrangian Grassmannian Λ(d) (a standard identification), the manifold #11 §10 (Λ(1), τ's circle) and §14 item 12 (Λ(4)) use; FLM treat it as a set of inequivalent choices, not as a vacuum manifold. Is the other choice equally lawful? In the flat theory, yes: T-duality J is a symmetry of the metastring action and exchanges the two Lagrangians (1502.08005 §2.4.1, §8); the dual description carries 'precisely the same information' (1707.00312 §3), and the string product is consistent with T-duality (§4). This matches #11 P5's 'the mirror vacuum is equally lawful'. Relative locality: different probes may carry different spacetimes ('different strings propagate in different space-time backgrounds', 1405.3949 §2; 'each string can carry a different space-time', 1502.08005 §2.3; metaparticles with different p̃ 'effectively experience different notions of space-time', 1812.10821 §2.1). My reading: this is the closest these papers come to #11 P4's matter in the other polarization, but it is a property of all probes, not a separate sector of matter, and nothing assigns ordinary matter to one Lagrangian and dark matter to the other. FLM's 'kinematical' describes the breaking by general relativity; their own proposal is a dynamical η without a selection mechanism. The program's spontaneous reading, with η as order parameter (#11 §3, P2′), has no counterpart here.
evidence: 1812.10821 §2, §2.1; all seven texts: zero matches for 'spontan' and 'order parameter'

answers.question: Q10
answers.answer: Not addressed. The only remark is that dynamical momentum space 'implies dramatic phenomenological consequences in the context of the vacuum energy problem [9]' (1405.3949 §1.3), citing Chang, Lewis, Minic, Takeuchi 2011 (arXiv:1106.0068) and Chang, Minic, Takeuchi 2010 (arXiv:1004.4220), whose abstract proposes 'a phenomenologically viable seesaw formula for the cosmological constant' (leads; abstracts only). No statement about w, the curvature of a dual spacetime as dark energy, a contracting partner universe or scale-factor duality; nothing to compare with #11 §10 (τ, w ≥ −1) or with C5 (#11 App. A item 9). 1502.08005 §8 names cosmology only as a future application.

answers.question: Q11
answers.answer: These papers do not state the identification and cite no earlier statement of it (no 'dark' in any text). As framework they all precede the program's first statement (September 2026): Born geometry, Born reciprocity as a choice of Lagrangian, and dynamical η (1307.7080, 26 July 2013); spacetime as a preferred basis broken by gravity, and dynamical η as 'our addition to Born's argument' (1405.3949, 15 May 2014); 'broken Born duality' and 'a dynamical question' (1502.08005, 27 February 2015); quantum space as a polarization, with x̃ = p/ε in quantum mechanics (1606.01829, 6 June 2016); [x, x̃] = 2πiλ² (1706.03305, 11 June 2017; 1707.00312, 2 July 2017); the metaparticle and its dual particle pair (1812.10821, 27 December 2018). For the program's own attributions, #11 §3 and P2′ cite 1502.08005; the 2013 letter and the 2014 essay are earlier statements of dynamical η and of a preferred polarization. Earlier sources FLM cite for the framework: Born (Nature 136, 1935; Proc. R. Soc. A165, 1938; Rev. Mod. Phys. 21, 1949), Snyder 1947 and Gol'fand 1960 (curved momentum space), Veneziano 1986 (Born reciprocity in string theory), Tseytlin 1990–91 (the action), Amelino-Camelia, Freidel, Kowalski-Glikman and Smolin 2011 (relative locality), and Aharonov's modular variables. None concerns dark matter.

answers.question: Other: which structure is rigid (#11 P2′ against the metastring)
answers.answer: #11 P2′: 'Only ω is rigid (symplectic rigidity ≡ constancy of ℏ). The neutral metric η is emergent', and it credits 'η dynamical' to metastring theory. The sources agree that η is dynamical but put quantum rigidity elsewhere: 'the rigidity of the quantum theory is encoded into the flatness of the polarization metric η', to be relaxed on general backgrounds (1502.08005 §1); the metastring promotes η, H and ω all to functions on phase space, keeping ω closed (§2.3); the string's symplectic form 'only depends on the neutral metric η' (§4.2), while ω is the symplectic form of the zero modes (1706.03305 §4.1). In ordinary quantum mechanics ω 'defines the Heisenberg algebra' (1606.01829), as in P2′. My reading: the program's rigid ω plays, for a point particle, the canonical role that η plays for the metastring's string modes; P2′'s 'η dynamical, as in metastring theory' is accurate for η, but the two frameworks hold different structures rigid. Whether a closed but position-dependent ω changes ℏ is not discussed in the papers (by Darboux's theorem such an ω is locally constant; my remark).

answers.question: Other: modular polarizations and #11 §3's mandatory breaking
answers.answer: #11 §3: '[x,p] = iℏ forbids joint locality, so any world with local physics must select a Lagrangian polarization. The magnet must point.' FLM show that the Heisenberg algebra also has polarizations that are not Lagrangian: maximal commutative subalgebras generated by modular variables, which 'commute with one another, and thus their eigenvalues can be specified precisely' (1502.08005 §7.2); 'generically, such polarizations contain a fundamental length scale', and the Schrödinger representation is 'a highly singular one' (1606.01829 abstract, §1.4). They also say modular observables evolve non-locally (1502.08005 §7.2) and that 'The concept of locality that we use in physical theories is tied to the choice of a preferred basis, the Schrödinger polarization' (1606.01829 §1.4). My reading: the premise holds for locality in the usual sense, but the alternatives are not only a Lagrangian polarization or joint locality: FLM's modular polarizations, with a finite cell of area ℏ, are a third option, which they propose as the quantum notion of space. #11 §3 does not discuss them. This bears on the program's framing, not on C1.

contradicts_record.record_says: review/wiki-build-flags.md item 64: "In their foundations the dual coordinates are the canonical conjugate of x (Freidel, Leigh and Minic, Phys. Lett. B 730, 302 (2014): "so we will refer to Y as coordinates in momentum space")." Also notes/literature-check.md §3, 'What their "dual" is': "The judge asked to argue for novelty found the duality the same, not a shared word: the school's dual coordinates are the canonical conjugate of x."
contradicts_record.why: Contradicts the wording, qualifies the substance. In the school's string papers the canonical conjugate of x is the ordinary momentum p ([x̂, p̂] = iℏ, 1706.03305 eq. 73). The letter's 'momentum space coordinate' Y is named for its period around the string, which is the momentum. Y is the T-dual field: its σ-derivative is the momentum density, and Y = X̃/α′ up to a function of τ, X̃ being 1706.03305's dual field (checked in scratch/r6-foundations/dual_field.py). Y's zero mode x̃ is a further variable: x̃ = q̃ + πα′p, with q̃ conjugate to the winding p̃ and commuting with x, so [x, x̃] = iπℏα′ (units.py). x̃ is momentum-like: it contains πα′ times p, in Y's momentum units [x, Y₀] = iπℏ, and FLM read (x, x̃) as a Heisenberg pair and the doubled space as a phase space. But it is not the canonical conjugate of x, and it is not the program's p, which stays a separate variable in these papers. Only FLM's paper on ordinary quantum mechanics, 1606.01829 §1.1, sets x̃ ≡ p/ε, the momentum of the same particle. Date: the letter was first posted 26 July 2013 (arXiv v1); 2014 is its journal year.

contradicts_record.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3, 'What their "dual" is': "In the foundations it is the momentum side." and "In the model their dark-matter statements rest on, the metaparticle, the dual coordinate x̃ is a coordinate of a doubled phase space at the string scale, with [x, x̃] = iλ², beside an ordinary momentum p with [x, p] = iħ = [x̃, p̃] (Hübsch and Minic 2024, §3). The identification matches C1 in their foundations; their model doubles phase space where the program polarizes one."
contradicts_record.source_says: 1502.08005 §2, eq. (13): "to unify both X^{\mu} and Y_{\mu} in one space {\cal{P}} (that we often refer to as phase space) and introduce a dimensionless coordinate \mathbb{X} on {\cal{P}}". 1706.03305 §2: "In particular, the zero modes (x,\tilde{x},p,\tilde{p}) should be considered independent, being linear combinations of (x_{L},p_{L},x_{R},p_{R}) ." 1707.00312 §2: "\omega_{AB} can be thought of as a symplectic form on the reduced space coordinatized by \mathbb{X}^{A} , a subspace of the full phase space." 1606.01829 §1.1: "introduce dimensionless coordinates x\equiv q/\lambda and \tilde{x}\equiv p/\varepsilon measuring position and momentum in natural units." 1812.10821 §2: "\{\tilde{x}_{\mu},x^{\nu}\}=\pi\alpha^{\prime}\delta_{\mu}^{\nu}".
contradicts_record.why: The doubling is not peculiar to the metaparticle: the string-theory foundations (1307.7080, 1502.08005, 1706.03305, 1707.00312) already work on the doubled target (X, Y) = (x, x̃) beside the momenta (p, p̃), the structure the metaparticle takes over from the string zero modes. The only FLM paper here in which the dual coordinate is the momentum of one undoubled phase space is 1606.01829, on ordinary quantum mechanics, not strings or dark matter. So the record's contrast, foundations (momentum side, matching C1) against model (doubled phase space), is in the sources a contrast between that one paper and the string papers. On the coefficient: the metaparticle paper's own bracket gives [x, x̃] = iπℏα′, which is 2πiλ² in 1706.03305's λ = √(ℏα′/2) and iπλ² in 1502.08005's λ² = α′ℏ; the record's iλ² (from Hübsch and Minic 2024, not read here) holds only in a normalization with λ² = πℏα′ (normalizations.py). 'At the string scale' depends on units: in the 2013 letter's momentum units the same commutator is iπℏ (units.py), and 1502.08005 fn. 32 says the cell's area is ℏ.

contradicts_record.record_says: papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md §3 (as in work/dual-sector/inputs/program.md): "They treat the breaking as kinematical and call the choice "a dynamical question"." Repeated in wiki/phase-space/reciprocity/broken-born-duality.md (opening): "they wrote no potential for η and treated the breaking as kinematical, not as spontaneous symmetry breaking."
contradicts_record.source_says: 1405.3949 §1.3: "Moreover, the purely kinematical splitting of phase space into space and momentum space has to be made dynamical, and thus both the phase space metric H_{AB} and the neutral metric \eta_{AB} have to be dynamical in the context of quantum gravity." 1405.3949 §1.1: "It is important to appreciate that this kinematical breaking is different from the dynamical breaking that arises in Schrödinger’s quantum mechanics, due to the choice of a particular Hamiltonian." 1502.08005 §8: "In the metastring formulation new CFT deformation modes are allowed, including the winding modes, whose collective excitations correspond to deformations of the \eta background."
contradicts_record.why: Qualifies. 'Kinematical' is FLM's word for the breaking by general relativity (and by the usual string, in which all probes share one spacetime). Their proposal is to make the split dynamical, with η a dynamical background deformed by string modes. So in their own framework they do not treat the breaking as kinematical; what they do not do is treat it as spontaneous: no potential for η, no order parameter, no vacuum selection (zero matches for 'spontan' and 'order parameter' in all seven full texts). The program's claimed addition, the spontaneous reading with η as order parameter, still has no counterpart in these papers; the description of what FLM did would read correctly as 'dynamical but not spontaneous'. The wiki page's other claims (η dynamical, no potential, no symmetry-breaking analysis) agree with the sources.

contradicts_record.record_says: papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md §4, P2′: "That η should be dynamical rather than fixed was argued independently in metastring theory [26S]; the reading of η as the order parameter of broken reciprocity is this program's." ([26S] = arXiv:1502.08005, posted 2015.) Also §3: "the idea that a preferred polarization breaks Born duality is Freidel, Leigh and Minic's ... [26S, p. 3]".
contradicts_record.source_says: 1307.7080 (arXiv v1 26 July 2013), Conclusion: "In this formulation both elements (\eta,J) of the chiral structure are dynamical. The solutions are labelled by bi-Lagrangians and spacetime is a derived dynamical concept." 1405.3949 (15 May 2014) §1.3: "Moreover if we introduce quantum theory in gravity, we have to make \eta dynamical. This is our addition to Born’s argument [1]." and §1.1: "There is a preferred basis — the space-time basis." 1502.08005 §2.1: "As we have pointed out in [3], in the metastring theory we must take \eta to be dynamical as well." 1502.08005 §1: "In the context of the metastring, the rigidity of the quantum theory is encoded into the flatness of the polarization metric \eta , a metric in phase space that tells us how to define the notion of Lagrangian submanifolds."
contradicts_record.why: Qualifies: the citation is correct but not the first statement, and the agreement is partial. 1502.08005 itself credits dynamical η to the 2013 letter; the 2014 essay states both dynamical η and the spacetime basis as a preferred basis broken by gravity. The earliest dated statements are 26 July 2013 (η dynamical) and 15 May 2014 (preferred basis; η dynamical as FLM's addition to Born). FLM put the rigidity of quantum theory in the flatness of η and promote η, H and ω all to functions on phase space (1502.08005 §2.3), while P2′ keeps ω as the one rigid structure (ℏ) and makes η emergent; in the metastring the string's symplectic form is built from η, not ω (§4.2). The two frameworks hold different structures rigid.

contradicts_record.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3, 'What differs': "The vacuum. #11's polarization is selected spontaneously (P5). ... The check found no such mechanism in the school's papers, where the classical spacetime label "corresponds to a choice" of polarization."
contradicts_record.source_says: 1502.08005 §7: "What is new about this viewpoint is that it allows us to think about the choice of space-time inside phase space as a dynamical question." and "The condition of L -projectability is a target space locality condition specifying which submanifold of {\cal{P}} can be understood as a space-time. What is conceptually remarkable here is that this target space locality condition is selected by demanding worldsheet locality." 1707.00312 §2: "Consequently, which compact coordinate, x or \tilde{x} , plays the role of a spatial coordinate depends on context." 1606.01829 §3: "A choice of quantum polarization is a choice of basis, unitarily equivalent to any other."
contradicts_record.why: Agrees that there is no spontaneous mechanism, but understates what the foundations say about the choice. (1) η is a dynamical field with string excitations (1502.08005 §1, §8). (2) Worldsheet locality selects the locality condition (projectability; quantum mechanically Λ-periodicity) that singles out a Lagrangian as spacetime (§6.4, §7). (3) For a compact string the compactification radius decides: x at large R, x̃ at small R (1707.00312 §2–§3; 1706.03305 §5). (4) In quantum mechanics a polarization is a basis choice, unitarily equivalent to any other (1606.01829). None is a vacuum that breaks a symmetry spontaneously: (2) is a consistency condition and (3) a modulus. Under (3) the selected polarization depends on a background parameter, unlike #11 P5's vacuum selection; under (4) the choice is not physical at all, unlike #11 §3's 'the magnet must point'.

contradicts_record.record_says: papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md §5, compatibility theorem: "Positive H satisfying both (η⁻¹H)² = 1 and (ω⁻¹H)² = −1 are exactly H = diag(g, g⁻¹), g ∈ Sym⁺(d)." Attribution: "It is the Born-geometry compatibility statement of Freidel, Leigh and Minic: writing the η-compatible H in terms of (G, B), H is related to ω through a complex structure exactly when B vanishes [26S, §2.1]."
contradicts_record.source_says: 1502.08005 §2.1: "In the string case if the B field vanishes H is related to \omega via a complex structure. This is no longer true if B does not vanish." 1502.08005 §2, footnote 9: "Here neutral means that \eta is of signature (d,d) , while H is of signature (2,2(d-1)) ." 1307.7080: "\eta is a neutral metric and H a generalized Lorentzian one".
contradicts_record.why: Minor qualification. The attributed content is confirmed verbatim, but in a different setting: FLM's H is Lorentzian, built from a Lorentzian G and B, while #11 §5 states the theorem for positive H with g ∈ Sym⁺(d). The algebra carries over, but FLM did not state it for positive H; the positive-H version is the program's adaptation of their statement.
